holidays.name: National Pencil Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the humble pencil, the tool behind countless doodles, exams, crosswords and great ideas. Dig out your favorite one, sharpen it, and write or sketch by hand.
holidays.origin: The day marks March 30, 1858. On that date, Hymen Lipman received a US patent for attaching an eraser to the end of a pencil.
holidays.funFact: Lipman sold his patent for a reported $100,000. The US Supreme Court later ruled it invalid, because combining two existing items was not a true invention.

holidays.name: National Turkey Neck Soup Day
holidays.description: This is a salute to one of the most overlooked cuts in the kitchen. Turkey necks simmer into a rich, deeply savory broth. It's a day for soup lovers and thrifty cooks to enjoy a hearty, old-fashioned bowl.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It celebrates the tradition of turning humble leftover cuts into comfort food.
holidays.funFact: Turkey necks are full of collagen and connective tissue. That is why they make such a silky, flavorful broth.

holidays.name: Grass Is Always Browner on the Other Side of the Fence Day
holidays.description: This is a cheeky twist on the famous saying. It invites you to stop envying your neighbor's lawn, or life, and appreciate what you have. Your own patch of grass may be fine.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial, tongue-in-cheek observance of unclear origin. It flips the old proverb about greener grass on its head.
holidays.funFact: The proverb about greener grass has been around for more than a century in various forms. Its roots go back to ancient Roman writing about crops in a neighbor's field.
